analysis:
Examined base text of docs/architecture/inference.md lines 798-1628 and the head-side patch (head 1030-1047). The diff only adds documentation for a new PromptTokenCache (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/PromptTokenCache.swift) that reuses tokenizer IDs for rendered-prompt pieces within the same prefix-cache scope, parallel encoding on up to four cores, linear-time ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma 4/GPT-OSS, load-time and sampled background equivalence checks with fallback to applyChatTemplate, and a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch. No source implementation is in this batch, so the claims are unverified.

Security relevance: this is a new in-process plaintext-derived cache (A-001, TB-007). It states reuse never crosses a cache scope (the coordinator-authored cacheSalt per T-041), which would keep cross-account exposure aligned with T-041/SEC-035. Integration should verify the following in PromptTokenCache.swift and LocalTokenizerBridge:
(a) The cache key actually includes the coordinator cacheSalt scope, and local/standalone requests without a scope do not share a global pool.
(b) Cached pieces stay in memory only, never touch disk or logs, and are bounded in size (memory DoS, T-016/T-029 class).
(c) Cache hits create no new same- or cross-scope TTFT timing oracle beyond SEC-035. Tokenization timing differences are a new, smaller timing channel that T-041 does not explicitly document.
(d) Template rewrites cannot alter the rendered text in a way that bypasses typed validation such as validateUserQuery or validateReasoningContext, and a mismatch disables reuse.
(e) Background comparisons do not retain plaintext longer than the request lifetime.

The threat model (T-041/T-028) may need a note covering this prompt-token cache surface. The docs-only evidence shows no concrete regression, so no finding is raised.
